# Slice 4 pre-flight audit — what already binds, and what it breaks

Baseline verified: `pytest` 169 passed, `adss check` all PASS (24 findings), against `warehouse.duckdb` as committed.

## Headline: three things that stop slice 4 as briefed

**H1 — a line has no date, and the generator can only date a stage by an attribute of its own entity.** This is a blocker, not a wrinkle. Verified by construction against a scratch copy of the model:

```
date_attribute: PLACED_ON on ORDER_LINE  ->  KeyError "ORDER_LINE has no attribute 'PLACED_ON'"
```

`read_uss` → `_refuse_measures_of_things_that_are_not_numbers` does `entity = model.entity(event.entity_id); entity.attribute(event.date_attribute_id)` (`src/adss/uss.py:210-214`), and `Entity.attribute` raises a bare `KeyError` (`src/adss/model.py:72`) — not a `UssError`, so the failure has no explanation attached to it. `_version_cte` then dates the row `cast(revision."<DATE>" AS DATE)` from that same entity's history view (`uss.py:223-252`). The walk inherits **keys only** and is **one hop** (`_stage_cte`, `uss.py:295-326`, iterating `model.edges_from(entity.id)`); it never carries a date.

The source confirms there is nothing to map from — live `$metadata`, fetched just now:

```xml
<EntityType Name="OrderDetail">
  <Key><PropertyRef Name="OrderId"/><PropertyRef Name="ProductId"/></Key>
  <Property Name="OrderId" Type="Edm.Int32"/><Property Name="ProductId" Type="Edm.Int32"/>
  <Property Name="UnitPrice" Type="Edm.Decimal" Nullable="false" Scale="Variable"/>
  <Property Name="Quantity" Type="Edm.Int16" Nullable="false"/>
  <Property Name="Discount" Type="Edm.Single" Nullable="false"/>
```

No date. And none of the three layers may go and get one: M1 forbids a join or subquery in `table:`; M5 forbids "a reach into another table" (`conventions.md:88,92`); a DAS contract has no key for an expression or a join (`contract.py:43-45`, ADR 0003). A second mapped table on the ORDER_LINE entity cannot help either — it would be keyed by `order_id`, which is not a line.

So the question *"revenue per order month"* forces a fourth decision the brief does not name, and it is bigger than the three that do:

| option | what it costs |
|---|---|
| generator learns to date a stage by a date reached along the walk | new DAR mechanism, new neutral fixture, new ADR — **exactly** what ADR 0007 refused to put in this slice: *"It also costs slice 4, where the expression vocabulary would have to grow … in the same slice that first exercises the fan-out property D-0001 is carried on. Two risky things at once."* (`0007…md:71-73`) |
| record `OrderDetails?$expand=Order` so the line's landed record carries the order date | `page_url` is hard-coded `?$count=true&$top=&$skip=` (`source.py:28-30`) — needs a new `Endpoint` field and a new contract key. Dotted `source_path` already works (`contract.py:140-144`, fixture `bad_duplicate_target.yaml:13` uses `Nested.ParentId`), so the extraction half is free. But it lands the same fact twice and gives PLACED_ON two homes — a B8 smell in the layer B8 governs |
| question joins `dar__uss."order"` and groups on `o.placed_on`, no calendar | the line event still needs *some* non-null date, so this does not actually escape; and ADR 0007 rejected the peripheral-as-of-now reasoning explicitly (`0007…md:93-96`) |

Whatever is chosen, it must be decided and recorded **before** the code (`conventions.md:202`), and slice 5 ("line to product to category", `questions/README.md:21`) inherits it.

**H2 — D-0001's exit condition cannot be met by slice 4.** Detail in §1 below.

**H3 — the composite-key collision the brief calls "live" is invisible in this data.** Measured over all 2155 real order lines: distinct keys *with* a separator = 2155; distinct keys *without* = 2155. OrderIds are 10248–11077 (five digits), ProductIds 1–77 (one or two), so no collision is reachable. A separator-less key passes every gate, every data check and both acceptance queries. Detail in §3.

---

## 1. D-0001 — what it commits slice 4 to, and its exit condition

The register is one table row, `docs/deviations.md:19`. Its **exit condition**, quoted whole:

> A second consumer needs isolation: a different shape of the same structure, or a group that must not see part of it. The generator then gains per-group projections over the same bridge and this entry is resolved

**That exit condition cannot be met by this slice, and saying so is the most useful thing in this report.** Slice 4 adds a fourth question to the same `destinations/app.py`, read by one more persona. A persona is not a consumer needing isolation: nothing in slice 4 needs a different shape of the bridge, and nothing must be hidden from anybody. There are no per-group projections to build and nothing to resolve. **D-0001 stays `open` after slice 4, correctly** — and the register's closing sentence ("An entry whose exit condition has been met and which is still open is a defect in the same way a failing test is") does *not* bite here.

What slice 4 **is** committed to is a **different, separately-stated obligation** in the Review paragraph (`deviations.md:44-53`):

> Each open entry is checked against its exit condition **and against whether its argument is still being carried on assertion** — D-0001's justification rests on measures not multiplying across a walk over many-to-one edges. Slice 2 built the first edge, so the walk is now exercised; the property it is supposed to protect is not, because both entities on that edge are at the same grain and no measure *can* multiply across it. The first measure at a finer grain arrives in slice 4, and that is where the argument stops being carried on assertion.

So the register asks two things of an open entry and slice 4 can discharge exactly one. The Why it must now make good on is D-0001's own middle clause: *"The structure being shared is additive by construction — keys inherit along many-to-one relationships, measures stay on the stage that owns them — so the fan trap R2 exists to prevent cannot occur in it."*

Concretely, after slice 4 the bridge holds 830 `placed` + 809 `shipped` + 2155 `taken` rows in one table, with freight non-null on 830 of them and revenue on 2155. If the deviation's argument is wrong, `q02` breaks (freight ≠ 64,942.69) — which makes **q01 and q02 continuing to pass the strongest cheap evidence available**, and it should be named as such in the slice's record rather than left as a side effect.

Also worth writing into the slice: the **cost** column already predicts its own first failure — *"a slice needing a measure defined one way for one reader and another way for another"*. Revenue is the classic case (gross vs net of discount vs net of freight). Slice 4 defines it once, for everyone, and that is the deviation being paid rather than a design choice.

## 2. ADR 0002 — is the fan-out test possible now, "exactly as 0002 describes it"?

0002 describes it twice. In the Decision Outcome (`0002…md:63-67`):

> This is what makes `sum()` additive at any grain the reader chooses, and it is proved by a test rather than trusted: **a fixture with two parents and three children**, where `sum(_measure__parent__…)` must still be the parent total and not three times it.

and in Confirmation (`0002…md:160-163`):

> **The fan-out test is not among them, and cannot be yet.** It needs two grains — parents and children — and this slice has one entity. It lands with the second grain, in the slice that first creates something for a measure to multiply across.

ADR 0006 repeats the deferral (`0006…md:233-237`): *"Both entities here are at the same grain … The first measure at a finer grain arrives in slice 4 … Saying so is the point: ADR 0002 asserted this property in slice 1 and it is still asserted now."*

**Answer: yes, it is possible — and it has been possible since slice 2, not slice 4.** Two facts, both checked:

- The test 0002 describes is over a **fixture**, and the fixture's grain is data the test invents. `tests/fixtures/dab/model.yaml` gained `CHILD`, `NEIGHBOUR` and the `CHILD_POINTS_AT_PARENT` edge in commit `cee95ff` (slice 2) — `git log -S'id: CHILD'`. `tests/fixtures/dab/uss.yaml` already declares measures on both PARENT (2 events) and CHILD. Nothing about the *repository's* model is needed to write "two parents and three children".
- The machinery suite already executes generated SQL against an in-memory DuckDB built from neutral fixture data: `tests/test_das_executes.py:64-97` creates a synthetic lake and runs the generated raw/staged/current views. So §6's *"Pure functions over data files. No warehouse, no network, no binary"* (`conventions.md:176`) is already read as "no **warehouse file**, no real build" — the precedent for the DAR equivalent exists and was set in slice 1.

What exists today instead is a **structural** proof, not a sum: `test_a_stage_that_does_not_own_a_measure_emits_a_typed_null_for_it` (`tests/test_uss.py:160-185`) asserts every non-owning branch emits `cast(NULL AS <type>)` for every measure it does not own. That is a strong assertion about the emitted text; it is not `sum(...)` over rows, and 0002's sentence promises the latter. Grep confirms no test anywhere sums a measure over two grains.

Two things to flag for the slice:

- If the fan-out test is written as a **data check** instead, §6:187 blocks the fixture form outright — *"A data check is never written against a stub or a fabricated warehouse."* So it must be over the real build, which means it must be **generated per measure from the model** (the way `relationship_checks` is, `checks.py:232-287`) — `checks.py`'s own docstring is the constraint: *"No SQL is written here and no source is named here."*
- Whichever form is chosen, ADR 0002's **Confirmation** paragraph then becomes false and must be edited. That is permitted, and only that: `conventions.md:210` — *"a record's Confirmation section is edited to match the checks that exist, at any time, and only ever to match them."* Its Decision Outcome sentence at `0002…md:63-67` is history and must be corrected in the new record, quoted (the precedent is ADR 0006's "Corrections to ADR 0002" and ADR 0008's "A correction to ADR 0002").

## 3. M1–M7 against a composite-keyed mapping; and the measure name

**M2 is the one that matters, and it is not mechanically checked.** `check_mapping` refuses only the *cardinality* half, and says so in its own docstring (`src/adss/mapping.py:140-146`):

> M2 is checked for cardinality here; its key-shape clause -- a concat without a separator collapses 'A1' + '23' and 'A12' + '3' into one key -- is review-only until there is a composite key to check.

The rule itself (`conventions.md:89`) permits *"a bare string column, `cast(col AS VARCHAR)`, or a `concat` of casts with a separator."*

**Measured, the collision is not live in this data.** Over all 2155 lines: `count(DISTINCT concat(cast(OrderId AS VARCHAR),'-',cast(ProductId AS VARCHAR)))` = 2155 and `count(DISTINCT concat(cast(OrderId AS VARCHAR),cast(ProductId AS VARCHAR)))` = **also 2155**. The brief's `121|3` vs `12|13` needs a four-digit order id; the real range is 10248–11077. So a separator-less key would be silently wrong-by-luck-only and **every gate, both acceptance queries and every data check would pass**. This is the same shape as slice 2's discovery that destination country equals customer country on all 830 orders (`questions/02…/question.md:66-83`, "The number is checked here. The mechanism is checked there"). The conclusion is the same: this slice should make M2's key-shape clause mechanical, because the data will never report it.

The ingredient is already written and needs no new machinery: `key_shape()` (`mapping.py:257-275`) preserves literals verbatim *specifically for this reason* (its comment at 269-270 quotes the `'A1' + '23'` case), and I verified its output —

```
concat(cast(order_id AS VARCHAR), '-', cast(product_id AS VARCHAR)) -> "concat(cast(? as varchar), '-', cast(? as varchar))"
concat(cast(order_id AS VARCHAR), cast(product_id AS VARCHAR))      -> "concat(cast(? as varchar), cast(? as varchar))"
```

Two adjacent traps, both verified:

- **A YAML flow sequence splits the concat on its own commas.** `primary_keys: [concat(cast(order_id AS VARCHAR), '-', cast(product_id AS VARCHAR))]` parses to `['concat(cast(order_id AS VARCHAR)', '-', 'cast(product_id AS VARCHAR))']` — three entries. M2's cardinality check *does* fire, but its message ("read as that many alternate identifiers") misdiagnoses. Block style or a quoted scalar both parse correctly. Note the stray-key detector that catches the same trap for attributes (`mapping.py:180-194`, and the comment in `order-mapping.yaml:19-24`) covers `attributes` only, not `primary_keys`.
- **`concat` swallows NULLs.** `concat(cast(NULL AS VARCHAR),'-',cast(3 AS VARCHAR))` = `'-3'`; `||` would give NULL. The source metadata does **not** mark `OrderId`/`ProductId` `Nullable="false"` on `OrderDetail` (unlike `UnitPrice`/`Quantity`/`Discount`). Today 0 of 2155 are null; a null one would manufacture a key rather than fail.

The rest of M1–M7 for `dab/mappings/order-line-mapping.yaml`:

| rule | verdict |
|---|---|
| M1 | `table: das__staged.order_details` ✓ — contract stem must be `order_details` (`conventions.md:40-41`: source entity set → snake_case plural) |
| M3 | `FULL_LOG` ✓ |
| M4 | `extracted_at` ✓ |
| M5 | `quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)` — I ran `reaching()` on it: **False**, accepted. ADR 0007 pre-authorised it in as many words (`0007…md:131-132`): *"slice 4's revenue follows the same rule without a new mechanism: quantity, price and discount are columns of one order line, and their product is arithmetic over that row"* |
| M5a | watch for `coalesce(discount, 0)` — forbidden (`conventions.md:93`). A null discount makes revenue null and `sum` skips it, silently |
| M6 | `ORDER_LINE_<VERB>_ORDER`; `source_table: das__staged.order_details` byte-identical; `target_transformation_expression: order_id` — shape `?`, matching ORDER's own key shape `?` ✓. Verified `ORDER_key` values are `'10248'` etc., so the engine's implicit int→varchar is applied identically on both sides |
| M7 | ✓ |

**§2 measure naming — it is already written down for you.** `conventions.md:119` is the worked example: `sum_revenue` → **`revenue_order_lines_amount`**. Descriptor `revenue`, entity part plural (`order_lines`, rule at :109), unit a real unit (`amount`, rule at :111), no scope or aggregation word (:110). With §1.3:76 the physical column is therefore **`_measure__order_line__revenue_order_lines_amount`** — entity singular in the prefix, plural inside the name, exactly as `_measure__order__placed_orders_count` already is. Confirmed by generating it (see §7).

The DAB *attribute* behind it is governed by §1.2, not §2 — precedent `SHIP_LAG_DAYS`/`SHIP_LAG_ORDERS_DAYS` and `FREIGHT_CHARGE`/`FREIGHT_ORDERS_AMOUNT`. So something like `REVENUE_AMOUNT`, not the measure's name.

## 4. §1.2 — the line entity and its attributes in business language

**"Line" is a business word here, and it is already this repository's chosen one.** The source's word is `OrderDetail(s)`; "line" appears nowhere in it. Conventions writes the name itself, three times, before the slice exists: `ORDER_LINE` as the example of a singular entity id (`:54`), `order_line` as the DAR object name (`:71`), `order_lines` as the plural measure part (`:109`), and `ORDER_LINE_ID` as the example of an entity-prefixed descriptive attribute (`:55`). Using `DETAAIL`/`DETAIL` anywhere in `dab/` would be the violation.

For the three source properties, the test is not "does the string appear in the source" but "was this name chosen from the business's vocabulary or copied from the source's". Every attribute in the model today was chosen: `OrderDate`→`PLACED_ON`, `ShipCountry`→`DESTINATION_COUNTRY`, `Freight`→`FREIGHT_CHARGE`, `CompanyName`→`TRADING_NAME`, `Country`→`BASED_IN_COUNTRY`, `CustomerId`→`CUSTOMER_CODE`, `OrderId`→`ORDER_NUMBER`. Note `FREIGHT_CHARGE` keeps the shared word "freight" — a word both vocabularies use is not a leak; the *name* is what must not be copied.

- `Quantity` → **`QUANTITY`** is safe and is §1.2:55's own example of an unprefixed generic attribute.
- `UnitPrice` → `UNIT_PRICE` would be the **first** attribute in this model that is the mechanical snake→UPPER of a source property (and byte-identical to the DAS column `unit_price`). §1.2:61 also asks for what a thing *is*, not how it is stored. The business fact is the price agreed *for this line on this order* — Northwind's `UnitPrice` on a detail is the price charged then, not the product's list price now — so a name that says that (e.g. `PRICE_EACH`, `AGREED_UNIT_PRICE`) is both more honest and safer. If `UNIT_PRICE` is chosen, argue it explicitly rather than defaulting into it.
- `Discount` → the business concept is the share of the agreed price not charged. `DISCOUNT_SHARE` / `DISCOUNT_RATE` says that; bare `DISCOUNT` is the source's word verbatim.
- The derived attribute: `REVENUE_AMOUNT` (or `REVENUE`), with a definition that states whether it is net of discount and gross of freight — that definition is the arbiter §6:191 will use when the two queries disagree.
- If `ORDER_LINE_ID` is added per §1.2:55, note it is the same expression as the primary key: the peripheral otherwise shows nothing about which order or product a line is (see §7).

## 5. §5/§6 — what may not appear under `src/` or `tests/`

`conventions.md:164` (hard): *"No data vocabulary anywhere under `src/` or in test code. No entity, attribute or business term from the model appears in the machinery or in a test."* `:189` (hard): *"No test contains an entity, attribute, measure, source or column name from the business … A per-question test function smuggles the vocabulary back in through its own name — so the runner is parameterised."*

A finer grain will tempt exactly these, and each is a violation:

- Any occurrence of `ORDER_LINE`, `order_details`, `product_id`, `discount`, `unit_price`, `revenue` under `src/` or `tests/`.
- A test named `test_revenue_is_not_multiplied_across_order_lines` — the function name is the leak.
- Writing the fan-out data check as literal SQL inside `checks.py`. Its module docstring is the rule: *"No SQL is written here and no source is named here. Every statement is a generated file, so the linter sees it and so the machinery works for a source it has never met."* The check must be **generated per measure/edge from the model**, like `relationship_checks` (`checks.py:232-287`).
- A special case in `uss.py` for "this entity is finer than that one". The generator has no cardinality and cannot get one (ADR 0006's finding: `cardinality:` is rejected, `type:` is dropped on compile). Any grain knowledge must come from the mapping's shape and be pinned by a check, per ADR 0006.
- `pytest.skip` / imperative `xfail()` (`:188`), or hand-editing `dar/uss/*.sql` (`:79`, blueprint R4).

What **is** legitimate machinery work, all of it generic and all of it needing a neutral fixture held as a data file: an M2 key-shape refusal in `mapping.py` (+ `tests/fixtures/mappings/bad_concat_without_separator.yaml`); a generated fan-out check in `checks.py`; and, if H1 is solved in the generator, an inherited-date mechanism plus a neutral fixture that exercises it. Note `destinations/` is neither `src/` nor test code — the page may and does name business columns.

## 6. §10, `question.py`, and whether the control is still worth anything

Mechanically checked, all in `check_question` (`src/adss/question.py:100-155`) and run by `tests/test_questions.py::test_every_question_in_this_repository_is_answerable`:

- every `{{token}}` in the prose **and** every `defines` entry resolves in `definitions()` (:102-111);
- control mentions none of `dab.`, `dab__`, `dar__uss` (:113-119) and **does** contain both `das__staged.` and `__current` (:120-125);
- answer contains `dar__uss` and none of `das__`, `dab.`, `dab__`, `read_parquet` (:127-137);
- both have an `ORDER BY` (:139-146);
- each declared dimension's last segment appears in the **answer** only (:148-155).

Comments are stripped first (`without_comments`, :56-58).

**Two staged views in the control is established, not new.** `q02/staged.sql:8-9` already does `das__staged.orders__current LEFT JOIN das__staged.customers__current`. Revenue's control is the same shape: `order_details__current` joined to `orders__current` for the month. Nothing refuses it.

**ADR 0005's shelf life has not expired.** The clause (`0005…md:119-122`):

> Bad, because the control query has a shelf life. It stays writable only while a question needs no integration; **from the first question spanning two sources**, writing it against the staged layer means reimplementing DAB inside the check. **Slice 6 is where that bill arrives**, and this record does not pay it.

The trigger is *two sources*, not two entity sets. Slice 4 spans two entity sets of one source — the same shape as slice 2. The bill is still slice 6's (`questions/README.md:22`: "**The second source.**").

But independence **degrades measurably**, and the question file should say so as q02 and q03 did:

- The control must now transcribe the revenue arithmetic that the mapping also contains. ADR 0007 already supplies the defence — the two are written from `dab/model.yaml`'s definition of the attribute, and §6:191 names that definition as the arbiter when they disagree. That defence only holds if the definition is written well enough to derive both from; it is the load-bearing sentence of the slice.
- The control's `INNER`/`LEFT` choice against `orders__current`, and the `WHERE order_date IS NOT NULL` mirroring the generator's event filter, are both now *reasoned* rather than obvious. Measured: all 2155 lines join to an order and all 830 orders have lines (1 to 25 lines each, mean 2.6), so both choices agree today and the agreement proves nothing about them. Say so, the way `q02/question.md:66-83` does.

## 7. The generated layer — exactly what the contract becomes

Computed by running `bridge_columns`/`bridge_sql`/`peripheral_sql` against a scratch copy of the model with `ORDER_LINE` appended (the entity last, one edge to ORDER, one sum measure). The new published contract, in order:

```
 0 _stage            5 order_key            8 _measure__order__placed_orders_count
 1 _event            6 customer_key         9 _measure__order__freight_orders_amount
 2 _event_date       7 order_line_key      10 _measure__order__shipped_orders_count
 3 _is_current                             11 _measure__order__ship_lag_orders_days
 4 _observed_at                            12 _measure__order_line__revenue_order_lines_amount
```

**It rearranges. `order_line_key` lands at index 7 and moves all four existing measure columns one place right.** `bridge_columns`'s docstring already tells the truth (`uss.py:378-392`): *"That grouping means the contract does NOT only ever grow at the end, and saying otherwise would be the more comfortable lie … because keys precede measures, every measure column moves right."* Three artefacts still say otherwise and slice 4 is where it becomes conspicuous:

- ADR 0002 driver (`:46`): *"a published column contract that a model change extends rather than rearranges"*;
- ADR 0002 consequence (`:124-125`): *"new entities and measures are appended, never inserted or renamed"*;
- `.claude/skills/dar/SKILL.md:25`: *"A model change **appends**; it never rearranges."*

Nothing catches it: `run_checks` derives `expected` from the same `bridge_columns()` it compares against (`checks.py:65-72`), so both sides move together. Nothing breaks either — §3:137 forbids `SELECT *`, and every question and the page name their columns. The ADR sentences are history → corrected in slice 4's record, quoted; the skill is not an ADR → just fix it. Also note the corollary: **where `ORDER_LINE` is placed in `dab/model.yaml` is part of the contract** — appended last moves only measures; inserted between ORDER and CUSTOMER would move `customer_key` too.

The ORDER_LINE branch, generated verbatim:

```sql
SELECT
    'order_line' AS _stage,
    'taken' AS _event,
    taken._event_date AS _event_date,
    TRUE AS _is_current,
    taken._observed_at AS _observed_at,
    taken.order_key AS order_key,
    cast(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS customer_key,
    taken.order_line_key AS order_line_key,
    cast(NULL AS BIGINT) AS _measure__order__placed_orders_count,
    ...
```

Two things to read off it: the line stage carries `order_key` and emits **`cast(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS customer_key`** — the walk is one hop, so **revenue cannot be grouped by customer country until slice 5's chain**; and every ORDER measure is a typed NULL on it, which is the fan-out property, in the emitted text.

**The peripheral for a composite-keyed entity** is unremarkable and that is the problem:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dar__uss.order_line AS
SELECT
    e."ORDER_LINE_key" AS order_line_key,
    e.eff_tmstp AS _observed_at,
    e."QUANTITY" AS quantity, ...
FROM dab."view_ORDER_LINE_hist" AS e
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY e."ORDER_LINE_key" ORDER BY e.eff_tmstp DESC) = 1;
```

`order_line_key` holds the concat string (`'10248-11'`); the components are **not** columns unless declared as DAB attributes, and the peripheral carries **no foreign key** — the only route from a line to its order is the bridge's inherited `order_key`. If the page wants to show a line, it needs `ORDER_LINE_ID` (and/or a product reference) declared as attributes.

Both generated files pass the repository's own linter (`sqlfluff lint` with `.sqlfluff`, clean). Longest emitted line is 117 of `max_line_length = 120`; `LT05` is excluded so length does not lint, but a longer measure id would push the self-alias past 120 and stop being one-screen readable.

One further gap this slice is the first to expose: **event ids are not unique across entities.** `_refuse_measures_that_would_share_a_name` keys on `(entity_id, measure_id)` (`uss.py:186-198`); nothing checks event ids. Declaring `PLACED` on ORDER_LINE too is accepted by `read_uss`, and fails only at `adss dar build` with `Parser Error: Duplicate CTE name "placed__version"` (reproduced). Loud, but late and misleading — and note all three existing questions filter on `_event` alone, which relies on a uniqueness nothing guarantees.

## 8. The engine and a concat key

**No probe artefacts exist in the repository** — I searched; the probe findings live only in ADR 0006, ADR 0004 and `.claude/skills/dab/SKILL.md`. What they say, and what remains unverified:

- The dab skill (`SKILL.md:42-44`) gives the exact form — *"Compose with `concat(cast(a AS VARCHAR), '-', cast(b AS VARCHAR))` — the separator is not cosmetic"* — but that is guidance, **not an observation**. Nothing in this repository has ever put an *expression* in `primary_keys`: both live mappings use a bare column (`order-mapping.yaml:10`, `customer-mapping.yaml:10`). Whether daana accepts an expression there, and how it embeds it in its generated key/window/pair SQL, is unverified against this engine on DuckDB. Given ADR 0006's precedent (a probe overturned two of ADR 0002's stated facts), **slice 4 should probe it before deciding**, in a scratch warehouse.
- Verified read-only against the built warehouse: `ORDER_key` is `VARCHAR` holding `'10248'` — the engine coerces a bare INTEGER column to the VARCHAR key. So `target_transformation_expression: order_id` on the new edge will produce byte-identical values to ORDER's own key. (Strictly, a bare *integer* column is not one of M2's three listed forms — a pre-existing looseness from slice 1 that slice 4 is the first to depend on.)
- Numeric attributes come back **`DECIMAL(28,8)`** whatever the source declared — confirmed on `view_ORDER_hist`: `SHIP_LAG_DAYS DECIMAL(28,8)`, `FREIGHT_CHARGE DECIMAL(28,8)`. This is the single most important fact for §9.
- The pair object will be `dab."ORDER_LINE_ORDER_x"` wrapped by `dab."v_ORDER_LINE_IS_LINE_OF_ORDER"`; `checks.py:132-136` builds `"{source}_{target}_x"` and will find it. The three generated relationship checks (`__one_target`, `__loaded`, `__resolves`) all parameterise cleanly over the new edge.
- The **DAS** side already handles a composite contract key: `current_view_sql` partitions by every primary key (`das.py:92`), and `key_check_sql` parenthesises them *specifically for this case* — `das.py:137-138`: *"count(DISTINCT a, b) is not a function DuckDB has, so a composite key would emit a check that cannot run."* Verified `count(DISTINCT (OrderId, ProductId))` = 2155.

## 9. The float, `checks.py`, and ADR 0007

`inexact()` (`checks.py:38-47`) reports any `float` among the values **either** query returns; a `Decimal` and a `bool` are exact. It is applied in `run_checks` to `(*control, *answer)` at `checks.py:183-191`, immediately before the row-by-row equality finding at `:192-201`.

**It fires at `adss check`, not at `pytest`.** ADR 0007 says so exactly (`0007…md:154-160`): *"`tests/test_exactness.py` pins the predicate … That runs on every commit. The predicate is then applied to both answers of every question by a data check in `run_checks`, which runs after `adss build` rather than in the gate — so a float-valued measure fails `adss check`, not `pytest`, and it fails on the values returned rather than on a column's declared type."* Confirmed: `test_exactness.py` only calls `inexact` as a pure function; `cli.py:331-342` is the only caller of `run_checks`.

What the float actually does, measured on all 2155 real lines:

| computation | result |
|---|---|
| `sum(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount))` as DOUBLE | `1265793.0395000004` → Python **`float`** |
| the same rows summed in reverse order | `1265793.0394999993` |
| per-row `cast(... AS DECIMAL(28,8))` then sum | `Decimal('1265793.03950000')` |
| `cast(sum(...) AS DECIMAL(28,8))` | `Decimal('1265793.03950000')` |

So ADR 0007's `[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]` warning is **not hypothetical at this scale**: the same 2155 values summed in two orders differ by 1.1e-9, and DuckDB imposes no order on `sum`.

Three consequences:

1. **The answer side is safe by construction, if and only if revenue is a DAB `NUMBER` attribute** (ADR 0007's option (a)). The engine stores it `DECIMAL(28,8)`, `_version_cte` emits `cast(... AS DECIMAL(28,8))`, and `sum` over DECIMAL is exact. Options (b) and (c) — a DAR expression, or the arithmetic in `uss.sql` — would carry the double into DAR and were already rejected (`0007…md:66-96`).
2. **The control is where it bites.** `staged.sql` reading `discount` as a DOUBLE and summing gives a `float`, and `adss check` fails on "both answers hold only exact values" before it ever compares the numbers.
3. **A cast silences the check without removing the float.** Wrap the control's `sum` in `cast(... AS DECIMAL(28,8))` (as q02 and q03 already do) and `inexact` is satisfied — but the arithmetic was still done in binary, and *where* the rounding happens is now a semantic choice: the answer rounds **per row** (DAB does), the control as written would round **the sum**. Round-then-sum ≠ sum-then-round in general. Measured per order month: 0 of 23 months differ today, and the double error (1e-9) sits one decimal digit below the `DECIMAL(28,8)` grid — a margin, not a guarantee. If the control casts, it should cast **per row**, so it rounds where DAB rounds; and the question file should record the measurement, the way `q03/question.md:65-74` recorded the same reasoning.

The decision upstream of all this is the **contract type for `Discount`**, and it is a genuine one. `ColumnType` (`contract.py:23-38`) is a closed vocabulary with `DOUBLE` and `DECIMAL` but no `FLOAT`/`REAL`, so `Edm.Single` has no exact landing type:

- **`DOUBLE`** is the honest reading of `Edm.Single` and keeps DAS from interpreting (S1), but puts a float in `das__staged` and hands the problem to every control query forever.
- **`DECIMAL(p,s)`** removes the float at the boundary. Verified the wire format supports it: the service renders `Discount` as decimal text (`0`, `0.05`, `0.15`, `0.2`, `0.25` — the only five values in 100 sampled records; eleven distinct across all 2155), and the payload is stored as a JSON string, so the text is what is cast. There is precedent for pinning what the source leaves unpinned — `orders.yaml:74`: *"Edm.Decimal with Scale=Variable. The scale is pinned here because the source does not pin it."* But `Edm.Single`→`DECIMAL` is a **re-type**, not a pin: if the service ever emitted `0.15000000596046448`, the cast would round it silently — an interpretation in the layer forbidden to make one.

Either way it is a decision with a cost, it belongs in the slice's ADR, and the contract's `description` must keep saying `Edm.Single` (`conventions.md:43`). Note also `UnitPrice` is `Edm.Decimal Scale=Variable` → pin precision/scale as `Freight` does, remembering `precision`/`scale` are their own keys (`contract.py:148-152`); and `Quantity` is `Edm.Int16`, which has no exact type in the vocabulary either — `INTEGER` is the nearest.

## 10. The third entity's effect on `destinations/app.py` and `adss shoot`

**`app.py` indexes positionally and has one hand-written cell block per question.** `q1 = asked[0]` (:127), `q2 = asked[1]` (:235), `q3 = asked[2] if len(asked) > 2 else asked[-1]` (:387). `asked` is `read_questions(...)` filtered to non-draft, non-superseded (:81-85), directory-sorted — so `04-…` lands at `asked[3]` and the existing three indices are undisturbed. Slice 4 must add a **new block of ~7 cells** (headline, chart(s), "What the words mean", `glossary(q4)`, row-count markdown, table), each wrapped in `shown(q4, …)`, with names nothing else defines — marimo builds its dependency graph from names, so reusing `a3`/`q3` breaks the page rather than the cell.

**The trap: `adss shoot` renders every question, including drafts; the page renders only the asked ones.** `cli.py:372` iterates `read_questions(project.questions)` **unfiltered**; `app.py:81-85` filters. So for any question that is `draft`/`superseded`, or `green` but without a cell block, `ADSS_QUESTION=<id>` makes `shown()` return `None` for *every* element (:45-51) and the page renders as the header markdown alone. `shoot()` then either raises `DestinationError` at the 20,000-byte floor (`destination.py:114-118`) or writes a near-blank `answer.png` **into `docs/questions/<dir>/`** (`cli.py:379-380`). Committing q04 as a draft, or committing it green before its cells exist, breaks `adss shoot` for the whole slice, not just for q04.

Three smaller things:

- `answers = {q.id: warehouse.execute(q.uss_sql).pl() for q in asked}` (:113) runs **every** question's `uss.sql` on every render, including the three single-question screenshots. Four queries per shot after slice 4; a cost, not a defect.
- The q3 block reads `a1` (`q3_placed = int(a1["placed_orders_count"].sum())`, :386) to compute the unshipped count. That cross-block dependency is already there and still resolves, because every question's answer is computed regardless of `only` — but it means the blocks are not independent and a q4 block should not add another such link.
- The revenue column arrives as a DuckDB `DECIMAL` and **altair cannot encode it** — cast to `pl.Float64` before charting, exactly as q02 does for freight (:238, with the comment at :236-237). That float lives only in the picture; keeping it out of `uss.sql` is what keeps §9's check exact.
